vignette: John, a 63-year-old publisher with Oceania heritage, has been dealing with the aftermath of a man-made disaster that occurred several months ago. The event, a massive explosion at his office building in downtown Los Angeles, resulted in multiple casualties and left John deeply traumatized. Since then, he has experienced a range of symptoms that have significantly impacted his daily life. The traumatic event began on what seemed like an ordinary day for John. As he walked into the conference room to discuss the latest book proposals with his team, there was a sudden loud noise followed by a blinding flash and intense heat. The chaos that ensued left John disoriented and shaken. He had managed to escape but witnessed several colleagues who did not make it out in time. Since then, every detail of the event remains vividly clear in his mind. John's nightmares have become frequent, leaving him waking up with a jolt, often gasping for air and drenched in sweat. These dreams are so realistic that he can almost feel the heat of the explosion again. During these moments, John feels on guard even inside his own home, never fully able to relax or let his guard down. Talking about the event is one of John's most significant triggers. He finds himself avoiding conversations with friends and colleagues who were also present during the disaster. When he does have to discuss it, the memories come flooding back in clear and detailed images. The smell of alcohol, which reminded him of the fire extinguishers used that day, now sends waves of anxiety through his body. John's daily life has been significantly altered by these experiences. At work, he constantly scans his environment for any signs of threat, often sitting with his back to a wall so he can see everything happening around him. He finds himself startled at ordinary sounds like the phone ringing or even someone closing a door, which would not bother most people. These behaviors have started to affect his relationships and professional life. John's friends have noticed that he avoids social gatherings, leading to strained friendships. At work, his heightened state of alertness has made it difficult for him to focus on tasks, often causing delays in projects. His wife has also observed the changes in his behavior, feeling concerned about how isolated he seems. Despite these challenges, John had managed to keep going until recently when a small incident at home triggered another intense episode. He woke up from a nightmare and found himself in a cold sweat, heart racing. The smell of alcohol from a bottle on the counter brought back vivid images of that day. This was the final straw for him; he realized that he needed help to manage these overwhelming experiences. John is most afraid of losing control again, feeling vulnerable in his own home, and being unable to function at work or maintain relationships. However, he also hopes for a way to regain some sense of normalcy and peace, to be able to live without constantly looking over his shoulder. His current state has brought him to seek help, hoping that with support, he can find a path towards healing and recovery.
